MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

L12·N1176unmasked layer
This neuron fires on small connective/continuation tokens that link or extend a preceding phrase or item — conjunctions "and"/"or", the appositive comma after a proper name, hyphenated modifier "-type", and the "well" of "as well" — i.e. a structural "additional item follows" position rather than a semantic category.

This neuron fires at syntactic junctures where a phrase/clause is closed off or the main clause resumes after an interposed modifier — e.g., the final period of a self-referential clause, the hyphen in a compound modifier, or the pronoun/preposition/conjunction that continues the sentence right after a comma-set phrase; it is suppressed on ordinary mid-phrase content words like "prepared", "you", appositive commas.

L12·N7017unmasked layer

This neuron gives weak, diffuse activation on words occupying the "extension" slot inside a noun phrase — pre-nominal modifiers/hedges or conjunctions sitting between a determiner (or first element) and the head noun/verb ("the *comforting* thought", "your *previous* commitments", "the *specifically* national content", "spring and *early* summer", "Livni *and* Eli Yishai", "which *might* bring"); it is strongly suppressed on compound pre-modifiers of the same shape ("*hassle*-free", "*vendor* neutral", "*that* spicy…", "like *most* will").
